# `app` library — command reference

The cross-app runtime: the stock mount and module system (api.js), shared UI chrome, the scene stack, tokens, the client store, and the bridge/player bricks. Every app page is served through this library.

Version 134 · Root: `newbound_core` · App `/app/`, boot control `app`

[← Index](README.md)

## Contents

| Control | Commands |
|---|---|
| `app` | [apps](#appappapps), [asset](#appappasset), [assets](#appappassets), [delete](#appappdelete), [deletelib](#appappdeletelib), [deviceid](#appappdeviceid), [eventoff](#appappeventoff), [eventon](#appappeventon), [events](#appappevents), [exec](#appappexec), [jsapi](#appappjsapi), [libs](#appapplibs), [login](#appapplogin), [newlib](#appappnewlib), [read](#appappread), [settings](#appappsettings), [spawn](#appappspawn), [timeroff](#appapptimeroff), [timeron](#appapptimeron), [uninstall](#appappuninstall), [unique_session_id](#appappunique_session_id), [write](#appappwrite) |
| `service` | [init](#appserviceinit), [test_path_traversal](#appservicetest_path_traversal) |
| `util` | [hash](#apputilhash), [init](#apputilinit), [zip](#apputilzip) |

Controls without commands: `api`, `appcard`, `appinfo`, `dial`, `home`, `list`, `list_item`, `login`, `scenedoc`, `sceneexpr`, `scenehost`, `sceneproject`, `scenetokens`, `select`, `shape`, `tokens`, `ui`, `ui_reference`, `webgl`.

## Control `app`

The app library's boot and COMMAND HOST for the platform's core verbs: read/write/exec, login and sessions, library/asset listing, event and timer registration, app management. Routed at /app/.

### app.app.apps

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONArray` · **Groups:** `anonymous` · **Readers:** `["anonymous"]`

Provides a detailed manifest of all installed applications. Each entry includes the application's active status and a comprehensive list of its exposed commands, detailing their descriptions, parameters, and required access groups.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/apps`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/apps"
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"apps","params":{}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-app-apps`

### app.app.delete

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Deletes a specific data item, identified by its `id`, from the `lib` library. The operation is performed only after successful authentication of the provided `nn_sessionid`, returning 'OK' on success or panicking if unauthorized.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | The "lib" parameter specifies the name of the library where a data item is stored. |
| `id` | String | yes | The "id" parameter identifies a specific data item within a library or database. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | A unique identifier for the user's session, crucial for authenticating the request to delete data items. This request metadata is provided automatically by the Newbound framework. Pass a placeholder value like null when calling from the front end. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/delete`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/delete" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=<lib>' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=<id>'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"delete","params":{"lib":"<lib>","id":"<id>"}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-app-delete`

**See also:** [deletelib](#appappdeletelib)

### app.app.eventon

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Registers an event listener for a specified application (`app`) and event (`event`). When triggered, this listener executes a designated command (`cmdid`) from a command library (`cmdlib`), returning "OK" upon successful registration.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | yes | The "id" parameter is a unique identifier for an event listener that allows it to be referenced and managed in the application. |
| `app` | String | yes | The "app" parameter is an object that represents the main application instance and provides access to its properties, methods, and event listeners. |
| `event` | String | yes | The "event" parameter is an object containing information about a specific action or occurrence that has taken place in the application, such as a user interaction or system event. |
| `cmdlib` | String | yes | The "cmdlib" parameter is a library of command-line interface functions and utilities in a programming language, providing common operations such as file handling, string manipulation, and system calls. |
| `cmdid` | String | yes | The "cmdid" parameter is a unique identifier assigned to a command in a command-line interface system, used to distinguish commands and execute them appropriately. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/eventon`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/eventon" \
  --data-urlencode 'id=<id>' \
  --data-urlencode 'app=<app>' \
  --data-urlencode 'event=<event>' \
  --data-urlencode 'cmdlib=<cmdlib>' \
  --data-urlencode 'cmdid=<cmdid>'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"eventon","params":{"id":"<id>","app":"<app>","event":"<event>","cmdlib":"<cmdlib>","cmdid":"<cmdid>"}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-app-eventon`

**See also:** [eventoff](#appappeventoff), [events](#appappevents)

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

### app.app.spawn

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

The `spawn` command executes a specified command (`cmd`) from a given library (`lib`) within the Newbound runtime. It launches this operation in a new process, applying provided control settings (`ctl`) and arguments (`args`), and returns the execution result as a `JSONObject`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | Specifies the name or identifier of the library to be targeted by the `newbound exec` command. This defines the operational context for subsequent control and command parameters. |
| `ctl` | String | yes | Specifies the name of the control within the designated library. It defines the specific operational scope for the subsequent command to be executed. |
| `cmd` | String | yes | Designates the specific command or function to be executed within the operational scope defined by the `lib` and `ctl` parameters. |
| `args` | JSONObject | yes | Provides a JSON object containing additional, structured arguments that will be passed to the designated command (`cmd`). This object is serialized to a string before execution by `newbound exec`. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/spawn`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/spawn" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=<lib>' \
  --data-urlencode 'ctl=<ctl>' \
  --data-urlencode 'cmd=<cmd>' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"spawn","params":{"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","cmd":"<cmd>","args":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-app-spawn`

**See also:** [settings](#appappsettings)

### app.app.write

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** `anonymous` · **Readers:** `[]`

Saves a record to the flowlang data store and returns the stored record FLAT (its fields at the response top level). Takes the String library name `lib`; the record id `id` (Any — a null id has one generated); the JSONObject `data` to store; the `readers` and `writers` group lists (Any) that gate read and write access; and the String `nn_sessionid`, request metadata the Newbound frame supplies automatically, used to authorize the write.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | The "lib" parameter represents the library where the data will be saved. |
| `id` | Any | no | Unique identifier for the record in the flowlang data store. Pass null to have one generated — the param is still required. |
| `data` | JSONObject | yes | The "data" parameter represents the actual content or information to store. |
| `readers` | Any | no | The "readers" parameter refers to the groups that have read access to this information. |
| `writers` | Any | no | The "writers" parameter refers to the groups that have write access to this information. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | The "nn_sessionid" parameter is a unique identifier for an individual's session. This request metadata is provided automatically by the Newbound framework. Pass a placeholder value like null when calling this command from javascript. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/write`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/write" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=<lib>' \
  --data-urlencode 'data={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"write","params":{"lib":"<lib>","data":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-app-write`

## Control `service`

Headless COMMAND HOST for app-level service startup (init runs at boot).

### app.service.init

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Initializes the Newbound backend, launching a comprehensive web server that handles incoming HTTP requests, manages user sessions, and facilitates real-time communication via WebSockets. Sessions come from the session_id query parameter, the sessionid cookie, or - only when config.properties has basicauth=true - an HTTP Basic Authorization header checked against the security users on every request (one reused session per user, kept in system.basic_sessions; valid Basic credentials override an anonymous or foreign cookie session). A command that declares an nn_method parameter is a protocol adapter: when it is denied, the listener answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic (Basic enabled and nobody logged in, or wrong credentials) or 403 (logged in but not in the command's groups; also every denial when Basic is off) instead of the JSON UNAUTHORIZED error in a 200 that ordinary commands keep. MULTIPART UPLOADS: each file part of a multipart/form-data POST is written as upload_&lt;n> (0600) inside a private per-request directory &lt;tmp>/newbound_uploads/&lt;random> (0700); the client's filename is never used as a path. The command receives the temp file's path under the part's name and the original name, reduced to a basename (safe_upload_name: no separators, "..", control characters or ':'), under &lt;name>_filename. The directory is removed when the request is finished, after the command has returned and the response is written - copy the file if it must outlive the request.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=app&id=swshmm183e1fda678j7&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=app' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=swshmm183e1fda678j7' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"app","id":"swshmm183e1fda678j7","args":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-service-init`

**See also:** [test_path_traversal](#appservicetest_path_traversal)

### app.service.test_path_traversal

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

No-network regression for the HTTP path traversal guard. Checks the shared rule app.service.init path_is_safe (no ".." component split on / and \, no NUL), that do_get answers 400 and names no file for traversal paths - raw, percent-encoded, encoded slash and backslash, on the static html route, the app html routes and the app.asset route - and that app.app.asset itself answers an empty path for them and for malformed paths while still resolving a normal asset. Takes no input, reads no file. Returns FLAT {status, all_ok, count, checks:[{check, ok, detail}]}. Admin-only.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=app&id=xizoou1a1ee719698t3&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=app' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=xizoou1a1ee719698t3' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"app","id":"xizoou1a1ee719698t3","args":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-service-test_path_traversal`

**See also:** [init](#appserviceinit)

## Control `util`

COMMAND HOST for utilities: hash and zip (plus init). Its UI is a test scratchpad.

### app.util.hash

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Computes the Blake2b512 hash of a specified file or recursively of a directory's contents, returning the result as a hexadecimal string.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | String | yes | The string path to a file or directory whose contents will be hashed using the Blake2b512 algorithm. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=app&id=vvkpms183664f4a8az3&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=app' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=vvkpms183664f4a8az3' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"file":"<file>"}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"app","id":"vvkpms183664f4a8az3","args":{"file":"<file>"}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-util-hash`

**See also:** [init](#apputilinit), [zip](#apputilzip)

### app.util.init

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Ensures an application's runtime configuration is initialized with a unique UUID and an X25519 key pair, persisting these essential details to a configuration file.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=app&id=owtstr1836628eb57u3&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=app' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=owtstr1836628eb57u3' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"app","id":"owtstr1836628eb57u3","args":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-util-init`

**See also:** [hash](#apputilhash), [zip](#apputilzip)

### app.util.zip

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `Boolean` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Generates a compressed zip archive from the contents of a specified source directory. The resulting archive is saved to the provided destination file path, returning true on success or false on failure.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `srcdir` | String | yes | The "srcdir" parameter specifies the source directory from which to create a zip archive. |
| `destfile` | String | yes | The "destfile" parameter specifies the name and location of the output zip archive file that will be created. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=app&id=gstgit18361479c7atc&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=app' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=gstgit18361479c7atc' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"srcdir":"<srcdir>","destfile":"<destfile>"}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"app","id":"gstgit18361479c7atc","args":{"srcdir":"<srcdir>","destfile":"<destfile>"}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `app-util-zip`

**See also:** [hash](#apputilhash), [init](#apputilinit)
